classes.advisory: Apply foliar fungicides such as azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin at first onset of rectangular lesions. Practice 2-year crop rotation and plow under crop residue to reduce fungal inocula.
classes.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Disease Advisory

classes.advisory: Apply mancozeb (2.5 g/L) or propiconazole (1 ml/L) when cinnamon-brown pustules appear on upper and lower leaf surfaces. Plant resistant hybrids during cool, humid seasons.
classes.source: ICAR-IIMR Technical Bulletin on Maize Diseases

classes.advisory: Spray chlorothalonil or mancozeb at 10-14 day intervals upon detecting cigar-shaped grayish lesions. Ensure balanced potash fertilization to increase plant tolerance.
classes.source: ICAR-IIMR Package of Practices for Maize

classes.advisory: Crop foliage shows robust vegetative vigor with no visual pathogen lesions. Maintain timely irrigation and monitor whorls for early Fall Armyworm egg masses.
Spray mancozeb (2 g/L) or chlorothalonil upon emergence of concentric target-board dark brown spots on older lower leaves. Avoid excessive overhead sprinkler irrigation in late afternoon.
classes.source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Disease Manual

classes.advisory: CRITICAL EMERGENCY: Apply systemic fungicide (Metalaxyl + Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb) immediately upon water-soaked pale lesions with white fungal down on leaf undersides. Burn infected foliage before harvest to prevent tuber rot.
classes.source: ICAR-CPRI Shimla Late Blight Alert System

classes.advisory: Potato canopy shows vibrant green color with healthy turgid stems. Continue earthing up tubers at 30 and 45 days after planting and maintain moisture balance.
Spray copper oxychloride (2.5 g/L) combined with streptocycline (100 ppm / 1 g in 10 L water). Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet. Disinfect trellising stakes.
classes.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Disease Guide

classes.advisory: Prune infected bottom leaves touching the soil. Spray azoxystrobin (1 ml/L) or mancozeb (2.5 g/L). Mulch soil with straw to prevent fungal spores splashing up onto foliage.
Spray dimethomorph (1 g/L) or cymoxanil + mancozeb immediately upon detection of dark brown water-soaked necrotic lesions. Remove and destroy infected vines away from field.
Improve greenhouse/polyhouse ventilation and reduce relative humidity below 85%. Apply difenoconazole (0.5 ml/L) or copper-based protective fungicide.
Remove severely spotted lower leaves. Spray chlorothalonil or copper hydroxide at 7-day intervals. Keep leaves dry by employing drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers.
Spray spiromesifen (1 ml/L) or abamectin (0.5 ml/L) under high pressure targeting the undersides of leaves. Introduce predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) in protected cultivation.
classes.source: ICAR-National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources (NBAIR)

classes.advisory: Apply pyraclostrobin or fluxapyroxad when circular brown necrotic lesions with dark concentric rings appear. Ensure adequate plant spacing for airflow.

Vector control: Spray imidacloprid (0.3 ml/L) or thiamethoxam (0.3 g/L) to control whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) populations. Install 15-20 yellow sticky traps per acre. Rouge out stunted cupped plants immediately.
Disinfect hands, pruning tools, and stakes with 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) or skim milk solution. Avoid smoking or handling tobacco near tomato plants as the virus is mechanically transmitted.
Foliage exhibits vigorous chlorophyll development, upright growth, and healthy trusses. Continue regular fertigation schedule and preventive pest scouting.
